text: Gusfield: n − 1 flows; min edge on the tree path.

A Gomory–Hu tree (最小割树) of an undirected weighted graph is a tree on the same vertices such that, for every pair u, v, the minimum u–v cut in the graph equals the smallest edge on the tree path u–v. It needs only n − 1 max-flow runs and then answers all n² min-cut queries.

Gusfield's simple construction: parent[i] = 1 for all i. For i = 2 … n: compute the min cut between i and parent[i] (weight w, side S containing i); set the tree edge (i, parent[i], w); for every j > i with parent[j] = parent[i] and j ∈ S, set parent[j] = i. No graph contraction needed (P4897).

Square node per block; round nodes on the path.

The block-cut tree (圆方树): for every vertex-biconnected block (进阶篇第12章) create a "square" node and connect it to the "round" nodes (original vertices) of the block. The result is a tree. Every simple path u–v in the graph uses exactly the blocks on the tree path between u and v, and the vertices that every u–v path must pass are the round nodes on that tree path.

So "how many vertices lie on all u–v paths" (道路相遇 P4320) = number of round nodes on the tree path = (path length in nodes + 1) / 2. Build it with the same Tarjan stack as vertex_bcc.cpp, creating a square node per popped block.

Checked in Python by the definition: a vertex w lies on every u–v path iff it is u, v, or deleting it disconnects them. On the tree, round and square nodes alternate, so a path with L edges has L/2 + 1 round nodes.
Residues mod the smallest step; count reachable totals.

Shortest paths modulo a number (同余最短路): which totals can be written as ax + by + cz with x, y, z ≥ 0? Work modulo a (the smallest step): for each residue r mod a, let d[r] = the smallest reachable total ≡ r. Then every d[r] + k·a is reachable too. The d[r] are shortest paths on a graph of a vertices: r → (r + b) mod a with weight b, r → (r + c) mod a with weight c.
Count reachable totals ≤ h: Σr (⌊(h − d[r]) / a⌋ + 1) over residues with d[r] ≤ h. Graph size a, not h, so h can be 2⁶³ (跳楼机 P3403: floors reachable from floor 1).
Checked against listing every reachable floor in Python. Using the smallest step as the modulus keeps the graph smallest.
The same idea answers "the largest total that cannot be made" (with gcd 1): max over r of d[r] − a.
MCS ordering; planar duality; preflow push.

A graph is chordal (弦图) if every cycle of length ≥ 4 has a chord. Equivalently it has a perfect elimination ordering: an order where each vertex's later neighbours form a clique. Maximum cardinality search (MCS): repeatedly number the unnumbered vertex with the most numbered neighbours; reversing that order gives a perfect elimination ordering exactly when the graph is chordal.
O(n + m).

On chordal graphs many hard problems become easy: the chromatic number equals the maximum clique, which is max over v of (1 + number of earlier-numbered neighbours in MCS order); greedy colouring along the perfect elimination order achieves it (神奇的国度 P3196).
A random chordal graph (each new vertex joined to a clique), checked against trying every colouring in Python. Labels only increase, so stale bucket entries are skipped instead of deleted.

Planar graphs and duality (平面图与对偶图): in a planar graph each face becomes a dual vertex and each edge a dual edge between its two faces. A minimum s–t cut in the planar graph equals a shortest path between the two outer faces in the dual, which turns huge grid min-cuts into Dijkstra (狼抓兔子 P4001).
HLPP (highest-label preflow push) is another max-flow algorithm, O(n²√m), occasionally needed when Dinic is too slow on dense graphs.
Reverse Dijkstra heuristic; A*.

k-th shortest path (k 短路 , walks may repeat vertices): run Dijkstra from t on the reversed graph to get h(v) = dist(v, t), an exact heuristic. Then run A* from s with key g + h(v): the i-th time t is popped, g is the i-th shortest path length. Each vertex needs to be expanded at most k times.

A* is O(k · m log) in the worst case and is what most solutions use. The guaranteed method builds the shortest-path tree to t; every path is the tree path plus a list of "side-track" edges with cost w + h(v) − h(u), kept in persistent leftist heaps (第5章), giving O((n + m) log m + k log k) (P2483).

Stoer–Wagner phases; cheapest edge per component.

Stoer–Wagner (全局最小割): the minimum cut over all ways to split an undirected graph into two nonempty parts, with no fixed source or sink. One phase grows a set A by repeatedly adding the vertex most tightly connected to A; the last two added, s and t, satisfy: the weight of t to the rest is the minimum s–t cut. Record it, merge s and t, repeat n − 1 times.
O(n³) with an adjacency matrix (O(nm + n² log n) with a heap). It beats running max flow n − 1 times, and the code is shorter (P5632).

Checked against trying all 2ⁿ − 2 splits in Python.

Borůvka: in each round, every component picks its cheapest outgoing edge, and all picked edges are added at once. Each round at least halves the number of components, so there are O(log n) rounds. Break ties by edge index so that the picked edges never form a cycle.

Its power is that a round only needs "the cheapest edge leaving each component", which can be found without listing the edges: on a complete graph with weight ai xor aj use a trie (CF888G Xor-MST), on points use geometry. That gives MSTs of graphs with n² implicit edges in O(n log² n).
Checked against Kruskal in Python on the same random graph.
Euler's formula for planar graphs (平面图欧拉公式): a connected planar graph drawn without crossings has V − E + F = 2 (F counts the outer face). With C connected components: V − E + F = 1 + C.
Consequences: a simple planar graph with V ≥ 3 has E ≤ 3V − 6 (and E ≤ 2V − 4 without triangles), so it is sparse, and its average degree is below 6.

Typical uses: count the regions cut out by segments or chords (build the planar graph: intersections become vertices, then F = E − V + C + 1), prove that a graph is not planar (K5: E = 10 > 9), and bound edge counts so O(E) algorithms on planar graphs are O(V). With the dual graph (第 4 节) it turns planar minimum cuts into shortest paths.

Key points to memorise
1. Gomory–Hu: n − 1 max flows; u–v min cut = min edge on the tree path.
2. Gusfield: parent = 1; cut (i, parent[i]); later j on i's side with same parent ⇒ parent[j] = i.
3. Block-cut tree: square node per block; must-pass vertices = round nodes on the path.
4. 同余最短路 : d[r] smallest total ≡ r (mod a); count Σ (h − d[r]) / a + 1.
5. Chordal: MCS order; χ = max clique = max (label + 1).
6. Planar min cut = shortest path in the dual.
7. k 短路 : h = dist to t (reverse Dijkstra); A* on g + h; i-th pop of t = i-th path.
8. Stoer–Wagner: add most-connected vertex; last one's weight = s–t cut; merge s, t.
9. Borůvka: every component takes its cheapest edge; O(log n) rounds; implicit edges.
10. Euler: V − E + F = 1 + C; simple planar ⇒ E ≤ 3V − 6.
